highlights.title: Nifty’s Sharp November Rally Gives India’s IPO Hopefuls a Tailwind
highlights.description: Firms have raised about $18.6 billion through IPOs this year, with a flurry of deals expected in December.

highlights.title: Counterpoint on China's AI Progress Under Chip Curbs
highlights.description: Wei Sun, Principal Analyst for AI at Counterpoint Research, discusses the outlook for Chinese internet giants and leading AI labs as updated US chip controls further restrict access to the advanced semiconductors needed to train frontier AI models. She speaks with Annabelle Droulers on Bloomberg: Tech Asia. (Source: Bloomberg)

highlights.title: Mahanadi Coalfields Set for Mumbai Debut After $969 Million IPO
highlights.description: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd., a unit of state-owned Coal India Ltd., is set to start trading Friday after its initial public offering in the first listing since India’s market regulator barred publishing so-called gray-market prices for IPO shares.

highlights.title: Android just had one of its worst quarters, and Apple is benefiting
highlights.description: Android just recorded its lowest-ever share for a third quarter, with Apple's iOS bucking the trend.

highlights.title: Samsung Galaxy A38 runs Geekbench, confirms its chipset
highlights.description: Samsung launched the Galaxy A37 in March and released it in April, so the company is now almost wrapping up the development of its successor, the A38, for a plausible early 2027 launch. The device has now been spotted in the Geekbench online database with the model number SM-A386B. This is the global model, and it's powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 7500 SoC, which in the specific prototype which ran the benchmark was paired with 6GB of RAM. highlights.description: Stocks are having a wild ride thanks to the Nvidia affair, but AI-linked exports and investment are still driving growth—for now.

highlights.title: China’s Industrial Profits Jump at Fastest Pace in Five Months
highlights.description: Earnings growth at China’s industrial enterprises hit a five-month high in October, as higher commodity costs and demand for artificial intelligence products continued to prop up prices.
